metadata.neutral_citation: NG KAM CHOU v. CHUNG YOI CHIU AND ANOTHER [1980] HKCFI 74; HCA 968/1978
metadata.case_name: NG KAM CHOU v. CHUNG YOI CHIU AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_after: clerk (worked in Urban Council library; later joined Tai Chong Motors as a clerk in the accounts department)

source: after the accident on the 8th of March 1974 the plaintiff had concussion and was at first treated in the General Surgical Unit at the Queen Mary Hospital and subsequently transferred to the Orthopaedic Unit on the 10th of March 1974.

He suffered a number of severe injuries; a dislocation of the right shoulder, a double fracture of the pelvis, a compound fracture of the right Tibia and Fibula (bones of the lower leg) and a fracture of the left Tibia.

injuries.description: double fracture of the pelvis (fracture of the wing or Ilium of the pelvis on the right and the Inferior Ramus of the Pubis)
injuries.body_part: pelvis (right ilium and inferior ramus of pubis)
source: X-Ray shows that he suffered a fracture of the wing or Ilium of the pelvis on the right and the Inferior Ramus of the Pubis. ... the whole hip region is slightly pushed inwards so that the right side of the Pelvis is mildly distorted, but the alteration of the position of the hip joint is very slight and the whole joint has moved in as a unit; the fractures did not involve the hip joint itself.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of pelvic bone without disruption of posterior arch of pelvic ring

injuries.description: compound fracture of the right Tibia and Fibula at mid-shaft; lower fragment of the Tibia displaced backwards by 1/2in
source: He fractured the right Tibia and Fibula at mid-shaft; the fractures are soundly united and the lower fragment of the Tibia is displaced backwards by 1/2in., but otherwise alignment is excellent and there is no angulation of the fragments on each other.

injuries.description: fracture of the left Tibia at mid-shaft (oblique fracture) well united
source: He also fractured the left Tibia at mid-shaft. The fracture was oblique and is well united and overall alignment is excellent.

injuries.description: probable small chip fracture of the Ulna at the elbow socket
source: X-Ray of the elbow shows that there was probably a small chip fracture of the Ulna (bone of the forearm on the 5th finger side) at the edge of the Ulna where it forms the socket of the elbow joint.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of upper end of ulna

injuries.description: mild degree of shortening of both legs (probably about 3/8ths of an inch)
source: The leg lengths are equal, but from studying the X-Rays I think he probably has a mild degree of shortening of both legs, probably about 3/8ths of an inch.

manifestations.description: cannot fully straighten the arm at the elbow (loss being 5°) and cannot bend it through 150°
15° deficit of flexion of the arm at the elbow compared to the left arm
lost 10° of the movement of supination; pronation is normal
some pain on severe pressure of the pelvic region
mild shortening of both legs (about 3/8ths of an inch)
can walk for up to half an hour, manage six flights of steps, run slowly
resumed going swimming (his main pre-accident recreational sport)

treatments_received: plaster casts from mid-thigh downwards for a number of months
transfer to Rehabilitation Centre at Kun Tong for a period of two months
physiotherapy and exercises (re-admitted for physiotherapy and exercises three times)
post-discharge physiotherapy at Sai Ying Pun Clinic three times a week for an unspecified period
use of two sticks for two months and one stick for a further month

losses.description: Pain, suffering and loss of amenities arising from multiple injuries including concussion, dislocation of the right shoulder, double fracture of the pelvis, compound fracture of the right tibia and fibula and fracture of the left tibia with small residual impairments (judge awarded general damages for pain, suffering and loss of amenities).

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Temporary inability to partake in strenuous activity; his main pre-accident recreational sport was swimming (he has resumed swimming but was not fit for strenuous activity for a period).

comparable_cases.case_name: Chow Yu v. Yuen Lam Hin and Another
comparable_cases.injury_description: The injuries in the first case were less severe and the pain and suffering would have been less but the residual injuries were worse.

comparable_cases.case_name: Chung Tai Hai alias Chung Yin v. Lau Kai Sun and Another
comparable_cases.injury_description: There would be a shorter period of hospitalization but some residual disability. The pain and suffering, however, would have been less than in the present case.

comparable_cases.case_name: Li Sai Hung v. Tsui Kwong Wai
comparable_cases.injury_description: There were no injuries to the hips but again the residual injuries would have been more severe and would have affected him more as he was a farmer.
